podcast.title: Too fast, too soon

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you do any sport? Guess: who in this episode ran twenty-one kilometres yesterday — Leyla or Sam?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is sport. And I can't walk properly today.
[laugh] Why not?
Yesterday I ran my first half marathon. Twenty-one kilometres.
Wow, congratulations! How was it?
The first ten kilometres were great. But I made a classic mistake. Everyone around me was running fast, so I ran fast too.
Oh no. You should never jump the gun in a long race.
I know that now. After fifteen kilometres I had no stamina left. I walked a lot of the last part.
But you finished! That's what matters. Did you warm up before the race?
For two minutes. My coach was not happy. He says a good warm-up protects you from injury.
He's right. At school I played tennis, and I hurt my knee because I never stretched.
Were you good?
Not really. But once I played in a school tournament, and I was the underdog. Everyone thought I'd lose in the first round.
And?
I got to the final! My opponent was a real athlete, much stronger than me. I said to myself: just give it your best shot.
Did you win?
[chuckle] No, I lost the final. And I still think the referee made a mistake on the last point.
Of course he did.
But it was the best day of my sporting life.
I love that. Next year I want to run the half marathon again and raise the bar — under two hours.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: have you ever been the underdog — in sport or in life? What happened?
Ask me again next year. See you next time!
Bye for now!
